title: define_froi ranks NaN vertices as MAXIMALLY selective; the chain then prints a confident NO-GO over a real effect
reasoning:
SURVIVES, and is partly UNDERSTATED. I reproduced every mechanical claim independently rather than trusting the evidence.

CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION:
- np.argsort places NaN last ascending; [::-1] puts it first. argsort([0,nan,5,1]) = [0,3,2,1], reversed [1,2,3,0]. NaN is ranked as maximally selective.
- define_froi(la, lb, parcel=arange(100,200), top_n=20) with la[150:170]+=0.5 and la[123]=nan returns an fROI containing vertex 123, displacing genuine vertex 155. Exactly as claimed.
- raw_roi_mean(np.array([[1.,nan,3.]]), arange(3)) -> nan. No finiteness check at line 204.
- u_statistic([nan]*4, [1,2,3,4]) -> 0.0 (both `f > s` and `f == s` are False for NaN; contributes nothing, raises nothing).
- perm_p([nan]*4, [nan]*4) -> 1.0.
- The "silently deleted observation" claim is exact, not approximate: exact_perm_p([1,2,3,nan],[.1,.2,.3,.4]) = 0.0285714 and exact_perm_p([1,2,3],[.1,.2,.3,.4]) = 0.0285714 — identical, while n is still reported as 4v4.

UNDERSTATED IN ONE PLACE: glm_contrast_z is worse than "missing an assertion." Line 494's `ok = se > 0` evaluates `nan > 0` as False, so NaN vertices are assigned z=0 and averaged into the ROI mean — silently diluting the contrast toward the null instead of propagating NaN. Verified: glm_contrast_z([[1,nan],[2,1]], [[0,1],[0,2]], [0,1]) = 1.5, the NaN vertex contributing a clean zero. Same bug class, quieter, in a function the fix only wants an assertion bolted onto.

MY LENS (attack the fix): the fix is correct and I could not break it. I applied it to the real file, ran the suite (32 passed), and confirmed (a) it raises naming the offending vertex, (b) it does NOT false-abort when non-finite values lie outside the parcel — critical, since a whole-array check over 20484 fsaverage5 vertices could kill valid runs on medial-wall values. I then tried to find a simpler or better fix and found the obvious one is a trap (see correction). The perf objection to the broader assertions does not hold: I timed an isfinite check in the worst placement (mc_perm_p inner loop) at 1.2x on a 4.7 ms call.

HONEST NARROWING ON IMPACT: define_froi currently has no production caller — grep finds it only in tests/test_roi_stats.py (2 tests) and ops/interface-contracts.md. The "pipeline prints NO-GO" chain is prospective, not an already-corrupted number. But MASTER-PLAN S2, the next GPU step and the paper's headline replication, specifies "Define the face fROI from half the exemplars, test on the other half," so this is one wiring step from load-bearing with 8 days to deadline. It is shipped tribe_tools/ library code with a published contract; any caller gets a silent wrong result. Severity stays critical — catching it pre-wiring is exactly what this audit is for, and the failure shape (confident negative from a broken statistic) is the 2026-07-31 retraction repeated.
correction:
The finding stands; three corrections to the PROPOSED FIX, plus one addition.

1. REJECT the tempting simpler fix. A reviewer will reach for `np.argsort(-sel)[:k]` as a one-character change. I verified it does exclude NaN (they sort last under negation) and returns only clean vertices — but SILENTLY, handing back a plausible k-vertex fROI from a corrupt localizer with no signal that anything was wrong. That is precisely the silent-absorption class this project retracted over. It also flips tie-breaking from highest-index to lowest-index (verified on an all-ties input: current picks [5,4,3], the alternative picks [0,1,2]), a silent ROI-composition change. Use the raise.

2. Use `np.isfinite(sel).all()`, not the finding's alternative `np.isfinite(a[pv]).all() and np.isfinite(b[pv]).all()`. I checked every non-finite input combination — nan-nan, inf-inf, inf-0 — and all propagate to a non-finite `sel`, so the single check is equivalent and simpler. Keep it scoped to `sel` (parcel vertices only): I confirmed a NaN outside the parcel correctly does NOT abort, which a whole-array check would.

Verified working form (32/32 tests still pass):
    sel = a[pv] - b[pv]
    if not np.isfinite(sel).all():
        bad = pv[~np.isfinite(sel)]
        raise ValueError(
            f"localizer has {bad.size} non-finite value(s) inside the parcel "
            f"(vertices {bad[:10].tolist()}) - np.argsort ranks NaN as the MOST "
            "selective value, so these would silently define the fROI"
        )
    keep = pv[np.argsort(sel)[::-1][:k]]

3. Drop event_locked_response from the list of places to guard — it is a thin wrapper. The check belongs in peri_event_timecourse where `roi = p[:, verts].mean(axis=1)` actually reads the data (line 351); that covers both entry points with one guard. In glm_contrast_z the check must be on the inputs `a[:, verts]` / `b[:, verts]`, NOT on `se` — guarding `se` would collide with the documented and intentional "zero pooled variance contributes 0" policy.

4. ADDITION the fix omits: glm_contrast_z needs more than an assertion. Its `ok = se > 0` mask (line 494) is itself a NaN swallower — see reasoning. Whatever guard is added, that mask should be written so non-finite se is distinguishable from zero-variance.

5. DOCTRINE: CLAUDE.md rule 2. ops/interface-contracts.md:447 documents Raises clauses for roi_minus_reference and detection_floor; the define_froi entry there must gain one in the same change. The fix as proposed does not mention updating the contract file.

No perf grounds to resist any of this: measured 1.2x on an isfinite check in the hottest possible location.

title: define_froi ranks with argsort()[::-1], which sorts NaN to the FRONT - a localizer with dead vertices returns an fROI made entirel
reasoning:
I set out to refute this and could only refute half of it. The core NaN claim is exactly what the code does, and the downstream consequence is worse than the finding states.

CODE (note: finding's line numbers are wrong — it is lines 539-540, not 387-389, of /home/deveshb/workspace/AI/tribe-bench/tribe_tools/roi_stats.py):
  sel = a[pv] - b[pv]
  keep = pv[np.argsort(sel)[::-1][:k]]
There is no isfinite guard anywhere in define_froi (lines 527-541). Confirmed numpy 2.5.1 puts NaN last ascending, so [::-1] puts it first.

REPRODUCED VERBATIM. define_froi with ten real selective vertices at 100-109 (value 1.0) and ten NaN at 150-159, parcel arange(100,200), top_n=10 returns [150...159] — the dead vertices, none of the ten real ones. Partial case (5 NaN) returns a 50/50 mix. -inf is handled correctly (sorts last); only NaN and +inf sort to the front.

THE FINDING IS UNDERSTATED ON THE SILENT-FAILURE AXIS. It says the held-out contrast "returns a null". I traced what kind of null. In an end-to-end S2-shaped simulation (genuine +1.5 sigma face effect at 100-109, dead NaN vertices at 150-159 present in BOTH localizer and test halves, split-half localizer, top_n=10):
  fROI chosen         -> [150..159]  (all dead)
  glm_contrast_z      -> exactly 0.0
  glm_contrast_z on the true fROI -> 3.013
  raw_roi_mean        -> nan
glm_contrast_z returns a clean, finite, unremarkable 0.0 with no NaN and no warning, because its own guard `ok = se > 0` evaluates False for NaN (nan > 0 is False) and leaves z=0 for those vertices. So the paper's headline non-compositional statistic — the Fig-4-comparable one the replacement rests on — silently reports "no selectivity" on a 3-sigma real effect. Per-clip route is equally silent: u_statistic on all-NaN arrays gives U=0.0 and perm_p=1.0, a maximally confident null. Only raw_roi_mean surfaces a visible nan.

QUANTIFIED DOSE-RESPONSE (parcel of 300, k=104, m dead vertices in parcel): every dead vertex is guaranteed a top slot, each contributing exactly 0 to the ROI z, so the estimator is biased toward zero by roughly (k-m)/k. m=5 -> z 1.23 falls to 1.00; m=52 -> 0.85; m>=k -> 0.07 (total null). The bias direction is always toward the null, which is the direction of the conclusion the paper intends to publish — the worst possible direction for a silent bias.

WHAT I COULD NOT SUBSTANTIATE, and why this stays major rather than critical: the NaN premise is unproven for this pipeline. There is no medial-wall masking code in tribe_tools (grep for nan/isfinite/medial across tribe_tools, ops/source-of-truth.md and data/algonauts finds only viz.py view names), TRIBE v2 predictions are a plain forward pass over all fsaverage5 vertices, and define_froi has no callers yet. Weak supporting evidence only: data/algonauts/their_parcel_centroids_mni.npy already carries 3 non-finite values, so non-finite data does circulate here. Also, in the one ROI configuration the docstring names (58-vertex Glasser right-FFC) the default top_n=100 caps k to the full parcel size, making the ranking inert — I verified the fROI is then the whole parcel. The bug only fires when top_n < parcel size, which is the intended S2 configuration (~104 vertices).

Against those mitigations: the guard is three lines; glm_contrast_z at line 468 explicitly documents and handles the exactly analogous degenerate-vertex case ("Vertices with zero pooled variance contribute 0 rather than inf"), so the omission in define_froi is an inconsistency rather than a considered choice; and silent failure is this project's declared signature bug class. Major is correct.

THE SECOND HALF DOES NOT SURVIVE. The flat/all-tied localizer complaint is real behaviour (define_froi(zeros, zeros, arange(100,200), top_n=8) returns [192..199] with no error, confirmed) but it does not matter here and the proposed fix is wrong. An exact all-tie across float TRIBE predictions has probability ~0; it arises only from synthetic zeros. More decisively, tests/test_roi_stats.py:407-409 (test_define_froi_caps_at_parcel_size) deliberately calls define_froi(np.zeros(10), np.zeros(10), parcel, top_n=100) and asserts only size==5 — the proposed "raise when the k-th and (k+1)-th values are tied at the max" would break that existing intentional test. Ties at the selection boundary are also legitimate in quantized or integer-valued localizers, so raising there would be a false alarm. Arbitrary-but-deterministic tie-breaking is standard for a top-N selector.
correction:
Narrow to the non-finite half only, and correct the location and the fix.

Location: tribe_tools/roi_stats.py lines 539-540 (the finding cites 387-389, which is event_locked_response).

Surviving claim: define_froi ranks with np.argsort(sel)[::-1] and has no isfinite guard, so any NaN (or +inf) in the localizer contrast is ranked as maximally A-selective and is guaranteed a slot in the fROI. Because the paired downstream statistic glm_contrast_z maps those vertices to z=0 via its `ok = se > 0` test (nan > 0 is False), the corruption is invisible: the ROI z is biased toward zero by approximately (k-m)/k for m dead vertices in the parcel, and becomes exactly 0.0 — finite, clean, no NaN, no warning — once m >= top_n. perm_p on all-NaN per-clip values returns 1.0. The bias is always toward the null, i.e. toward the paper's intended conclusion.

Dropped: the flat/all-tied-localizer claim and its proposed tie-raising fix. Degenerate synthetic-only input, deterministic output, and the proposed fix would break the existing intentional test tests/test_roi_stats.py:407-409.

Precondition to check before this is worth fixing at all (cheap, and it decides urgency): assert np.isfinite on the actual S2 localizer arrays. If TRIBE predictions are finite everywhere on the parcels in play, this never fires. No masking code in tribe_tools currently produces NaN.

Corrected fix: in define_froi, after `sel = a[pv] - b[pv]`, add
  finite = np.isfinite(sel)
  if not finite.all(): raise ValueError(f"localizer has {int((~finite).sum())} non-finite vertices in the parcel")
Raising is preferable to silently restricting to the finite subset, because a localizer with dead vertices in the target parcel is a data problem the operator must see before S2 runs. Add one test for the NaN case. Separately worth logging as its own item (out of this finding's scope): glm_contrast_z silently absorbs non-finite vertices as z=0, which is what converts this into a silent failure rather than a loud one — a NaN there should propagate or raise, not become 0. Also note the default top_n=100 exceeds the 58-vertex right-FFC parcel, making define_froi a no-op in that configuration.

title: glm_contrast_z has zero value coverage — replacing its entire body with `return 0.0` passes all 32 tests
reasoning:
The factual core is TRUE and I reproduced it independently: neither glm test constrains the return value. `test_glm_contrast_z_is_unmoved_by_a_distant_region` is tautological — glm_contrast_z's first computational line is `av, bv = a[:, verts], b[:, verts]` (roi_stats.py:488) and the test mutates `a2[:, 200:]` while `roi = np.arange(0, 50)`, so it perturbs columns the function provably never reads. On a clean tree, replacing the body from line 488 to the end with `return 0.0` gives "46 passed in 4.78s". The shipped implementation is correct (matches per-vertex scipy ttest_ind(equal_var=True) averaged over the ROI to 1.8e-15 at equal n, exactly 0.0 at unequal n 9v17).

But the finding's severity rests entirely on a concrete failure that I REFUTED by running it. It claims a 2.449x scale error "would silently rescale the glm_contrast_z column of data/floor_table_v3b.md and make the paper's cross-statistic floor comparison wrong by a factor of 2.4". That column does not contain the statistic's values — it contains the MDE in RAW FFCr-effect units, obtained from a permutation test on the statistic (detection_floor_table.py:71-88). With N_PER_GROUP=15 on both sides, both cited surviving mutants (`se = np.sqrt(var)` and `ddof=0`) are strictly positive CONSTANT rescalings, so obs and all 500 permuted values scale identically and the p-value is exactly invariant. Measured on the real pipeline (build_brain + clip_map, D_AUD=0.24, N=15, 500 perms), at effects 0.0/0.01/0.02/0.03: orig p = 0.305389 / 0.029940 / 0.001996 / 0.001996, and BOTH mutants return those same p-values to the last digit (only obs differs: 0.2178 vs 0.0795 vs 0.2255 at effect 0). Same power curves, same interpolated floor, byte-identical table. Nothing in data/floor_table_v3b.md can be corrupted this way. More generally the only shipped consumer tests glm_contrast_z by permutation, so it is invariant to ANY strictly monotone rescaling — exactly the error class the finding's mutants and its proposed scipy oracle target. The `z[~ok] = diff[~ok]` mutant is also inert: zero pooled variance does not occur on continuous simulated data.

The one mutant that DOES move the table (`return 0.0`) is not silent. obs=0 makes every permuted value tie, so p=1.0 at every effect size and the glm_contrast_z column prints 0.00 power at all 11 rows with floor "> 0.30 (not reached)" sitting next to raw_roi_mean's 1.00 — unmissable in the very artifact the script exists to produce.

It still survives, narrowly, because one live consumer does read the VALUE rather than its rank: MASTER-PLAN S2 line 392, "Contrast per §3.1 exactly. Also compute `glm_contrast_z`. Report both." And ops/interface-contracts.md:443 marks the function "⚠ OPEN … Under audit", so it is the single function most likely to be rewritten in the next eight days, with no value oracle to catch a df or scale slip during that edit. That is a real, cheap-to-close gap — but it is a prospective test-hygiene gap on verified-correct code whose only current output path neutralises the demonstrated error class, not a critical defect. Note also that the proposed scipy oracle would PIN the current across-observations two-sample form, which several other audit lanes propose to replace with the paper's across-time GLM; it is a lock as much as a check, and should be written as a hand-computed known-value case plus a zero-variance case rather than only a self-similar scipy comparison.

Environment note, reportable per rule 5: no search of mine failed, but parallel lanes are mutating tribe_tools/roi_stats.py live. I found and restored a foreign leftover mutant (`_resolve_rows` default `tol=91.5` instead of 0.5, which was failing test_event_locked_response_is_loud_when_a_time_has_no_row), and a second foreign mutant (raw_roi_mean `mean` -> `np.median`) appeared after my final `git checkout --`, which I left in place. My checkout may have disturbed another lane's in-flight mutation run.

However, the claimed impact is wrong: the statistic's ONLY shipped consumer (scripts/detection_floor_table.py:71-88) tests it by permutation and reports floors in raw effect units, so it is exactly invariant to any monotone rescaling — I verified that both cited "surviving" mutants (`se = np.sqrt(var)`, `ddof=0`) reproduce the original p-values to the last digit at four effect sizes, i.e. data/floor_table_v3b.md is unchanged by the very error the finding says would corrupt it, and the `return 0.0` mutant fails loudly (a full column of 0.00 power). The residual exposure is limited to MASTER-PLAN S2's "Also compute glm_contrast_z. title: glm_contrast_z is attributed to the paper's Fig 4, but §5.9 says the visual contrasts use no GLM and the paper's GLM is a differen
reasoning:
I tried to kill this and could not. Attacking the claim itself, in three parts:

1. IS THE CODE WHAT THE FINDING SAYS? Yes, exactly. /home/deveshb/workspace/AI/tribe-bench/tribe_tools/roi_stats.py:458-495. Docstring line 461 verbatim: "What Meta's Fig 4 actually reports, and non-compositional." Body: diff of condition means over a pooled two-sample SE across OBSERVATION ROWS, meaned over ROI vertices. No design matrix, no regressors, no HRF convolution, no whitening, no time dimension at all. The finding's quoted lines are correct character-for-character.

2. IS THE ATTRIBUTION FALSE? Yes, and — importantly — it is false under BOTH readings of the paper, so the finding does not actually depend on its §5.9 quote being right. I fetched arXiv:2605.04326 myself and verified the Fig 4 caption verbatim: "Experimental images are flashed for 1 second, with an interval of 8 seconds, and a general linear model (GLM) is fit on the predicted time-series to obtain z-scored contrast maps (see section 5.9 for details)." A GLM fit on a predicted TIME-SERIES is not a two-sample z over clip rows. And under the §5.9 reading, the paper's visual contrast is the plain t=5 subtraction — also not this estimator. Either way, "what Meta's Fig 4 actually reports" is false as written.

The §5.9 visual quote is additionally corroborated inside this repo, independently of the finding: MASTER-PLAN.md:145 quotes the visual method as "the predicted response at t=5 after the image is shown … subtracting the average responses at t=5 for the other categories" — wording that does NOT appear in the Fig 4 caption, so it came from the methods text. MASTER-PLAN §3.1 already flags the caption/methods tension with a ⚠. So the caption-vs-§5.9 discrepancy is real and already half-recorded.

3. IS IT ALREADY KNOWN / HARMLESS? This is where I expected it to die, and it doesn't. ops/interface-contracts.md:443-446 says of this exact function: "⚠ OPEN: MASTER-PLAN §3.1 describes Meta's Fig 4 GLM z as effect/SE across TIME per vertex. This implements across-OBSERVATIONS. Under audit." So the project's own contract file records the attribution as UNRESOLVED while the shipped docstring — and D027, the decision the paper will be written from ("what the paper's Fig 4 reports") — state it as settled fact. The shipped artifact overclaims relative to the project's own record. That is not a theoretical imperfection; it is the sentence a reviewer will check against a caption I have now verified says something else, in a paper whose entire subject is a statistic that was retracted for being asserted rather than checked.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY, and am flagging rather than endorsing: two WebFetch attempts (arxiv.org/html and ar5iv) both truncated before §5.9 — the section is listed in the ToC as "In-silico experiments" with separate "Visual experiments", "Language experiments", "Contrast maps", "Regions of interest" paragraphs, but I never saw its body. So the finding's nilearn FirstLevelModel / AR(1) / hrf_model='glover' detail is UNVERIFIED by me. It is plausible and structurally consistent, but it must not be written into ops/source-of-truth.md as VERIFIED on this finding's say-so — that would repeat the exact error being corrected. Someone must read §5.9 directly (PDF) before recording it.

WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE: the "must never be tested against 1.96" clause is a real property but a non-defect here. I reproduced it (null sd 0.2314 at 20 independent vertices, 15v15, seed 0 — matching the claimed 0.230; and 1.02 when vertices are perfectly correlated, so the null sd is somewhere in [1/sqrt(n_v), 1] depending on inter-vertex correlation). But grep over tribe_tools/, tests/ and scripts/ finds no comparison of glm_contrast_z to any critical value; scripts/detection_floor_table.py:75-88 correctly permutes it. So that leg is a docstring improvement, not a defect.

Net: real, cheap to fix, and it is the paper's central methodological sentence. It corrupts a published CLAIM rather than a published NUMBER — no computed value is wrong — which is why I keep it at major rather than raising it.
correction:
Narrowed to what is independently established:

title: glm_contrast_z uses a pooled (equal-variance) SE; at unequal n its permutation test is not level-alpha in either direction

TYPE I — CONFIRMED, MAGNITUDE ROUGHLY AS CLAIMED. So the distortion only bites once the sd ratio reaches roughly 1.5 or 0.67; it is not a knife edge.

The finding says Case B "reports NO-GO no matter how large the real face effect is" and calls it "the same class of error as the retracted spatial_z result". It is not. I measured it: at the finding's own worst case (na=50, nb=200, sd_a/sd_b = 1/3) the pooled test's power is 0.000 at delta=0, but 0.130 at 0.15, 0.330 at 0.20, 0.860 at 0.30 and 1.000 at 0.50. MDE at 80% power is ~0.29 pooled vs ~0.20 Welch — a ~45% inflation of the detection floor, not blindness. spatial_z was categorically worse: it INVERTED a genuine effect (p=0.9985 on a real 0.05 effect). Equating the two overstates this by a wide margin.

REALISTIC S2 CONFIGURATION IS MILDER STILL. At a more plausible 0.25-0.5 spread, pooled Type I is 0.014/0.008 and the two are nearly indistinguishable. So the structurally-guaranteed direction (pooled arm more variable) costs 20-30% of MDE, not the paper.

(3) The unequal-n premise is an inference, not a fact of the codebase: MASTER-PLAN specifies EQUAL exemplar counts per category (>=50 each, or 25 each across 5). title: glm_contrast_z's `se > 0` mask silently converts NaN vertices to z = 0 and does not implement the zero-variance guard it documents
reasoning:
I attacked the claim on its own terms and re-derived everything from scratch with different seeds. Both mechanisms reproduce, and the second is worse than the finding states.

NaN half, CONFIRMED exactly. `ok = se > 0` is False for NaN, so the vertex retains its initialized z=0 and stays in the z.mean() denominator. My run: clean 5-vertex ROI z=15.398; one NaN sample at a[3,2] -> 12.336; the entire vertex NaN -> 12.336, bit-identical. One corrupted sample is numerically indistinguishable from a dead vertex, and both are indistinguishable from a true-null vertex (z=0 is exactly the null expectation). No exception, no warning, finite output.

An asymmetry the finding did not claim, which strengthens it: on identical NaN-bearing input, raw_roi_mean, roi_minus_reference and spatial_z all return nan (loud, propagating, catchable). glm_contrast_z alone returns a plausible finite number. Every sibling statistic has an implicit NaN tripwire; this one defeats it.

Variance half, UNDERSTATED. The finding says you need ~1 ULP of jitter. You do not. numpy's var(ddof=1) of a genuinely constant column is not zero when the value's mean is not exactly representable: np.full(15, 0.7).var(ddof=1) = 1.32e-32 (same for 0.2, 0.1, 0.3, 1.7, 2.4). On a 58-vertex FFCr-sized ROI, clean z = 13.977; adding one exactly-constant vertex (0.7 in A, 0.2 in B) gives 2.60e14. The docstring's guarantee "vertices with zero pooled variance contribute 0 rather than inf" is false in the exact case it names. It holds only for constant-ZERO vertices (var exactly 0), i.e. the likely medial-wall case, so the guard works precisely where it is least needed. This is not attenuation but annihilation: one degenerate vertex out of 58 dominates the ROI mean entirely.

Where I narrowed it. The finding's failure narrative targets scripts/detection_floor_table.py. That corruption is not currently realizable. I ran the actual simulation path (build_brain / clip_map, 10 reps of the v3b design, n=15/group, FFCr=58): zero NaNs, minimum se = 1.196e-02, ten orders of magnitude clear of the danger zone. A clean grep across all 8 files in tribe_tools/ (exit 1, completed normally, no truncation) finds no NaN production or handling anywhere in the library. All 32 tests pass. So no already-computed number is wrong; the harm is prospective, not retrospective.

Why it still survives despite that. The bar is "real AND produces a silent wrong result." This is a silent-wrong-result mechanism in the primary replacement for a retracted statistic, in a project whose stated signature bug class is silent failure. MASTER-PLAN.md:392 schedules S2 to compute glm_contrast_z on real TRIBE predictions and report it alongside the sec. 3.1 contrast; that has not run yet, and it is the first time this statistic meets non-synthetic data, eight days from the deadline. Separately and independently of any data pathology, the docstring affirmatively asserts a guarantee the code does not provide, so an auditor checking the degenerate-vertex case is told "handled" when a constant vertex actually yields 1e14. Wrong contract text in the file the paper rests on is itself the defect.

Not critical: nothing published is currently corrupted and the trigger requires data the pipeline has not been shown to produce. Not minor: the failure is undetectable when it occurs, its magnitude is unbounded in the variance case, and the one defense the codebase has (NaN propagation) is defeated for exactly this function.
correction:
The finding stands, with three adjustments.

1. STRENGTHEN the zero-variance half. It is not limited to "constant only up to float32 rounding (se ~ 1e-17)". A genuinely constant vertex already breaks the documented guarantee, because np.var(ddof=1) of a constant column is nonzero (~1e-32) whenever the value's mean is not exactly representable in binary: np.full(15, 0.7).var(ddof=1) = 1.32e-32. Verified magnitude on a realistic 58-vertex ROI: clean z = 13.977 -> 2.60e14 with one constant vertex. Important carve-out: a constant-ZERO vertex is safe (var is exactly 0.0, guard fires correctly), so the medial-wall / dead-vertex case most likely to occur in fsaverage5 output is the one case that works. The exposure is a constant NONZERO vertex, e.g. a saturated or bias-only readout unit.

2. ADD the silence asymmetry, which is the strongest argument for the "silent" lane. On identical NaN-bearing input, raw_roi_mean, roi_minus_reference and spatial_z all return nan; glm_contrast_z alone returns a finite plausible number. The project's de facto NaN detector is failure-by-propagation in the other statistics, and this function is the single hole in it.

3. NARROW the failure narrative. The claimed corruption of scripts/detection_floor_table.py is not currently realizable and should not be asserted as an active harm: on the real simulation path (build_brain / clip_map, v3b design, 10 reps) there are no NaNs and the minimum se is 1.196e-02. No NaN is produced or handled anywhere in tribe_tools (clean grep over 8 files, exit 1). The correct framing is prospective: the exposure opens when MASTER-PLAN.md:392 runs glm_contrast_z on real TRIBE predictions in S2, plus the standing defect that the docstring states a guarantee the code does not honor.

Also minor: attenuation is not exactly k/58. Zeroing a vertex removes that vertex's own z from the sum, so k/58 holds only in expectation over vertices of equal effect. My run: 15.398 -> 12.336 on 5 vertices, where 4/5 * 15.398 = 12.318.

The proposed fix is sound in shape. Two refinements: the finiteness check should run on the ROI slices av/bv rather than the full arrays, so that NaN in an irrelevant vertex outside the ROI does not raise; and the relative degeneracy test should be scaled by the data magnitude rather than diff alone, e.g. compare se against eps * max(1.0, abs(av).max(), abs(bv).max()), since diff itself is near zero for a vertex that is constant in both conditions and would make the threshold vanish.

title: glm_contrast_z is documented and named as a z-score but its null SD ranges from 0.14 to 1.06 depending only on inter-vertex correl

Report both" for FFC-right, PPA, EBA, VWFA and V1. Nothing in the code or tests prevents that. This is a live trap, not a theoretical one.

Two parts of the finding do not hold and I have narrowed them. (1) Its failure narrative asserts "with realistic TRIBE prediction correlation the ROI statistic's null width is well under 1". The rho~0.15 I measured is an artifact of the toy brain's independent per-vertex noise term, not evidence about TRIBE. The honest claim is that the scale is undefined and unmeasured, and wrong in either direction — conservative if rho is low, anti-conservative (6% nominal 5%) if rho is near 1. (2) Its top-end figure 1.057 exceeds the theoretical ceiling sqrt(28/26) = 1.038; immaterial but it should not be pinned in a test as written.

correction:

title: event_locked_contrast silently drops empty other-category arrays, changing the baseline denominator without notice

Without it you get `nan` plus two RuntimeWarnings ("Mean of empty slice", "invalid value encountered in scalar divide"). So the filter is not preventing a crash — it is converting a visible nan into a plausible finite number. That is precisely the failure class this file was written to eliminate; every other new function in it raises loudly (`row_times_from_segments` on a bad object, `_resolve_rows` on an unmatched time, `peri_event_timecourse` on zero onsets, `roi_minus_reference` on ROI/reference overlap, `glm_contrast_z` on n=1). WHAT I REFUTED — the failure narrative is mostly wrong. Two of the three named upstream causes cannot produce an empty array, because the library's own producer refuses to:
  - "a manifest typo" / category with zero onsets -> `event_locked_response` -> `peri_event_timecourse` raises ValueError("no event onsets given"). Confirmed by running.
  - "a category with all onsets outside the window" -> `_resolve_rows` raises IndexError("N of M requested times have no prediction row within 0.5 s"). Confirmed by running.
So the only live path is a caller that builds per-category arrays by label-masking a response vector (`resp[labels == c]`) instead of calling `event_locked_response` per category. No such caller exists: grep over scripts/, tribe_tools/, tests/, ops/, .notes/ finds the symbol only in its own definition, the docstring cross-reference at :43, two tests, and the plan/contract docs. S2 is unwritten. The branch is currently dead.

MAGNITUDE — the finding's 25% is a toy-example artifact, but the realistic number is not negligible either. At the 5-category S2 design (faces vs bodies/places/objects/characters, K=4 others) dropping the lowest category shifts the contrast by (m_dropped - mean_rest)/K; with plausible category means I get ~3%, which would not flip a permutation test. In that configuration K=2, and losing one category replaces the baseline with a single category's mean — a distortion of tens of percent, i.e. genuinely conclusion-capable. The severity therefore rests on a design choice that is still open, not on a settled one.

VERDICT: real, correctly described at the code level, currently unreachable through the library's own API, but a one-line latent trap in the function the S2 caller will be written against in the next ten days, in a file whose entire design contract is "never return a plausible wrong number". title: detection_floor reports a solvable configuration error as a scientific conclusion when alpha < 1/(n_perm+1)
reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not refute the mechanism, only its stated blast radius.

RE-DERIVED, ALL CONFIRMED:
1. `mc_perm_p` returns `(ge + 1) / (n_perm + 1)` (roi_stats.py:160), floor 1/(n_perm+1). `detection_floor.achieved_power` (roi_stats.py:585-593) tests `mc_perm_p(...) <= alpha`. If alpha < 1/(n_perm+1) the comparison is unsatisfiable, achieved_power is identically 0, and the bracketing loop (roi_stats.py:596-606) doubles hi from noise_sd to >1e6 (~21 doublings) and raises.
2. Validation at roi_stats.py:536-541 checks only `0 < alpha < 1`. There is no alpha-vs-n_perm check anywhere. Confirmed by reading.
3. Ran it: `detection_floor(30, noise_sd=1.0, alpha=0.004, n_sim=5, n_perm=200)` raises in 0.36 s with exactly the quoted text, including "the design is underpowered for any plausible effect; report that, do not run it". The design is not underpowered — analytic two-sample MDE at n=30/group, alpha=0.004, 80% power is ~0.90 sd (the finding says 0.79; either way it is ~1 sd, not >1e6). Raising alpha to 0.006 (just above 1/201 = 0.004975) makes the same call return a finite floor of 1.06. So the trigger is precisely the n_perm boundary, not the design.
4. Boundary arithmetic checks out: 1/401 = 0.0024938. `detection_floor(15, sd=1, alpha=0.025/6=0.004167, n_perm=400)` returns 1.369 (no raise); `alpha=0.001, n_perm=400` raises. So the crossover is where the finding says it is.
5. The message omits `n_perm` — the one parameter at fault — from the parameters it prints, which is what makes it actively misdirecting rather than merely terse.

WHERE THE FINDING OVERREACHES (why it stays minor, not higher):
- It is loud, never silent. It raises; it does not return a wrong floor. Nothing can be quietly published from it.
- No publication path touches it. `scripts/detection_floor_table.py` — the script that actually writes `data/floor_table_v3b.md` — does not import or call `detection_floor`; it rolls its own grid + `interpolate_floor` at ALPHA=0.025, N_PERM=500. Grep across scripts/, tribe_tools/, neurocheck/, brainlens/ finds only the definition, one docstring cross-reference (line 45), and tests/test_roi_stats.py:412-418 (which use alpha default 0.025 with n_perm=200, boundary 0.004975 — safely clear). Callers: zero.
- The stated failure scenario (5-6 ROIs x 2 IUT contrasts Bonferroni'd to 0.0025) contradicts the project's own doctrine. `iut_pass` (roi_stats.py:171-178) states the IUT "controls the family-wise error at alpha without further correction", and the pre-registered level is alpha=0.025 (detection_floor_table.py:41). Bonferroni over >=11 tests is not this project's declared regime, so that specific route is speculative.

WHAT KEEPS IT ALIVE ANYWAY: a realistic non-exotic trigger exists that the finding did not name. `n_perm` is a pure compute knob on a machine with borrowed CPU-only compute, and lowering it to speed up a floor scan silently invalidates strict alphas: `alpha=0.005` (the "redefine significance" level) with `n_perm=100` (boundary 0.0099) raises the same false verdict, as does `alpha=0.001` at the default n_perm=400. An operator exploring a stricter threshold, in a project whose doctrine is "no verdict without a floor", is told in the imperative that the design is hopeless and to report that. That is a diagnostic making a false scientific assertion, which is worth two lines of guard ten days out.

ALSO: the proposed fix is right but incomplete, and its advice is wrong in one case. The achievable-p bound is max(1/(n_perm+1), ~1/C(2n,n)) — the rank permutation null has its own floor from the design. Verified: at n=3/group, C(6,3)=20, perfect separation yields p ~= 0.040-0.048 at every n_perm I tried (20, 100, 400, 5000), so `detection_floor(3, sd=1, alpha=0.025, n_perm=400)` raises and there the message is TRUE — no n_perm helps. The proposed guard would not fire there (1/401 < 0.025), leaving that case as-is (harmless, message is correct); but at n=3 with n_perm=20 the guard WOULD fire and advise "increase n_perm to at least 40", which is actively wrong advice for a design that can never reach 0.025.
correction:
Narrower, corrected statement:

`detection_floor` never validates `alpha` against the smallest p-value its own test can return. When `alpha < 1/(n_perm+1)`, `achieved_power` is identically zero, the bracketing loop doubles to `max_effect`, and the RuntimeError at roi_stats.py:601-606 asserts "the design is underpowered for any plausible effect; report that, do not run it" while omitting `n_perm` — the parameter actually at fault — from the parameters it prints. The design is typically fine (n=30/group at alpha=0.004 has an analytic MDE of ~0.9 sd).

Impact is a MISLEADING DIAGNOSTIC, not a corrupted number: it raises loudly, and no publication script calls it today (`scripts/detection_floor_table.py` implements its own power grid and never imports `detection_floor`; the only callers in the repo are two tests). The finding's Bonferroni-over-10-ROIs scenario also runs against the project's own IUT doctrine (roi_stats.py:171-178, "without further correction") and the pre-registered alpha=0.025. The realistic trigger is instead an operator lowering `n_perm` to save CPU while scanning a strict alpha — e.g. alpha=0.005 with n_perm=100, or alpha=0.001 with the default n_perm=400 — both of which I confirmed raise the false message.

The fix should guard both floors, not just n_perm, and must not give impossible advice:

    min_mc = 1.0 / (n_perm + 1)
    min_exact = 1.0 / comb(2 * n_per_group, n_per_group)
    if alpha < min_exact:
        raise ValueError(
            f"alpha={alpha} is below the smallest p-value a label permutation test can "
            f"reach at n={n_per_group} per group (1/C({2*n_per_group},{n_per_group})="
            f"{min_exact:.2e}); no n_perm fixes this — the DESIGN cannot detect anything "
            f"at this alpha."
        )
    if alpha <= min_mc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"alpha={alpha} is at or below mc_perm_p's smallest return value "
            f"1/(n_perm+1)={min_mc:.6f}; this is a resolution limit of n_perm, not a "
            f"property of the design — raise n_perm to at least {int(np.ceil(1/alpha))}."
        )

The two branches matter: at n=3/group, perfect separation yields p ~= 0.04-0.05 at every n_perm from 20 to 5000, so the finding's single-branch fix would tell that user to raise n_perm when nothing would help.

1. Harm envelope. No production caller. scripts/detection_floor_table.py — the script that generates the paper's floor table — does NOT call detection_floor at all; it builds its own EFFECTS grid and uses its own local interpolate_floor. The only repo callers are tests/test_roi_stats.py:412-419, which pass noise_sd=1.0/2.0 with explicit tol=0.02. correction:
Narrower, substantiated version: `detection_floor`'s absolute default `tol=1e-3` truncates the bisection when `noise_sd` is small, silently returning the raw doubling bracket. Verified at n=15/n_sim=60/n_perm=200/seed=0: sd=0.001 returns 0.002 against a true MDE of 0.001118 (79% high), sd=0.002 returns 0.003 against 0.002234 (34% high). Because the inner test is rank-based (Mann-Whitney U), the power surface is exactly scale-invariant, so the true MDE is exactly 1.118 * noise_sd and the 2x return is unambiguously a truncation artifact.

BUT the defect only bites for noise_sd below ~0.003. At the statistic scales actually measured in this project the error is 0.7% and irrelevant: raw_roi_mean sd=0.0233 -> 0.026213 vs true 0.026032; roi_minus_reference sd=0.016 -> 0.018000 vs true 0.017876. The error direction is conservative (overstates the floor), so it can never produce a false detection claim. Fix as proposed: default `tol=None` -> `tol = 1e-2 * noise_sd`, and return or log the achieved bracket width so a skipped refinement is visible.

title: detection_floor reports a floor to more precision than the simulation supports, and misdiagnoses an n_perm resolution limit as an

PART (a) — REFUTED, on three independent grounds.

1. The stated mechanism is wrong. The claim is that `tol` "can be set far below the Monte-Carlo noise ... so bisection converges precisely on one noisy realization," with the fix being to clamp `tol`. I reproduced the finding's exact numbers (`detection_floor(15, noise_sd=0.02, n_sim=100, n_perm=300, tol=1e-4)` over seeds 0-4 gives [0.02125, 0.022734, 0.023047, 0.023828, 0.023516], spread 11.3%), then varied `tol` while holding everything else fixed:
   tol=1e-4, n_sim=100 -> spread 11.3%
   tol=1e-3, n_sim=100 -> spread 13.5%
   tol=2e-3, n_sim=100 -> spread 16.0%
   Coarsening `tol` by 20x makes the seed spread LARGER, not smaller. `tol` is not the driver and the proposed fix would make the reported problem worse. The driver is `n_sim`: holding tol=1e-3, n_sim=100 -> 13.5%, n_sim=200 -> 5.6%, n_sim=800 -> 5.6%. Note the finding ran at n_sim=100, half the default of 200; at the actual default the spread is 5.6% (0.0219-0.0231).

2. The failure narrative is factually false. It says "scripts/detection_floor_table.py prints floors to four decimals" driven by this bisection. That script never calls `detection_floor` — I read all 187 lines and grepped every caller. Its imports are `glm_contrast_z, perm_p, raw_roi_mean, roi_minus_reference, spatial_z`; its floors come from its own `interpolate_floor()` over a fixed EFFECTS grid at N_SIM=2000 permutations=500. The only callers of `detection_floor` anywhere in the repo are `tests/test_roi_stats.py:414-418`. So there is no path by which `tol` precision reaches a printed paper number.

3. What remains is generic Monte-Carlo error in a simulation-based MDE, and the function is explicitly seeded and documented as such ("seed: RNG seed. Reproducibility is required — the floor goes in the paper"). `achieved_power` re-seeds from `seed` on every call, so it uses common random numbers across effect sizes and is bit-reproducible. A rerun at the same seed gives the identical number; a different seed giving a different estimate is a property of every simulated power analysis, not a defect in this code. That is "theoretically imperfect but harmless here."

PART (b) — REAL, reproduced, survives.

`detection_floor` calls `mc_perm_p`, whose smallest attainable value is (0+1)/(n_perm+1). With alpha < 1/(n_perm+1), `achieved_power` is identically 0 at every effect, the doubling bracket runs to `max_effect`, and it raises text that blames the design:
  detection_floor(15, noise_sd=1.0, alpha=0.002, n_sim=20, n_perm=400)
  -> RuntimeError: "...the design is underpowered for any plausible effect; report that, do not run it"
1/401 = 0.002494 > 0.002. The design is in fact fine: the same call with n_perm=4000 returns a floor of 1.52 in 9 s. So the binding constraint is the permutation count, and the message names the wrong cause in a sentence written to be pasted into a write-up.

I confirmed the finding's own control is right, which is what makes the message untrustworthy rather than merely imprecise: at n=2 (comb(4,2)=6, min attainable p ~0.169) and n=3 (comb(6,3)=20, ~0.052) the same message is correct — discreteness really is the limit at alpha=0.025. title: define_froi returns a plausible-looking fROI from a zero-information localizer, biased to the parcel's highest vertex indices
reasoning:
MECHANISM: verified exactly, independently. define_froi is at roi_stats.py:499 (finding says 388 — stale line number). The operative line is `keep = pv[np.argsort(sel)[::-1][:k]]`. I reproduced both cited calls byte-for-byte on numpy 2.5.1: define_froi(x,x,arange(120),top_n=10) and define_froi(zeros(200),zeros(200),arange(120),top_n=10) both return [110..119], no exception, no warning. The shape guard at 531-532 passes trivially when both arrays are the same object. So the claim is not wrong and not overstated on the mechanics.

WHAT THE TAIL BIAS ACTUALLY IS: not "highest vertex indices" as a property of the vertex numbering, but the TAIL OF parcel_verts IN ITS GIVEN ORDER. With a shuffled parcel I got [13,14,29,50,57,62,76,86,107,116] — exactly pv[-10:] sorted, i.e. the last ten positions of the array as passed. Because a Glasser parcel is conventionally handed over sorted ascending, the finding's practical statement holds, but the invariant is positional, not anatomical.

TRIGGER PROBABILITY: low. grep across tribe_tools/tests/scripts/ops/.notes shows define_froi has NO production caller — only tests/test_roi_stats.py:398-409. Intended use per MASTER-PLAN S2 is "define the face fROI from half the exemplars, test on the other half", where loc_a and loc_b are distinct float32 prediction arrays; ties in a continuous contrast are measure-zero. Reaching the degenerate branch requires an upstream mistake (passing the same half twice, or an all-zero mask).

WHAT IT CANNOT DO — this materially narrows the blast radius. If loc_a is loc_b, the resulting fROI is still selected INDEPENDENTLY OF THE TEST DATA. It is therefore not double dipping and cannot manufacture selectivity or inflate a p-value. Downstream statistics remain honest tests of an arbitrary sub-region. The failure mode is a wrong-region / underpowered result, i.e. a spurious NO-GO — not the false-positive class. The finding's "every downstream statistic then reports honest-looking numbers" is right; its implied severity of corruption is not.

WHY IT STILL SURVIVES: a spurious NO-GO is precisely this project's retraction-class error. The 2026-07-31 headline that was pulled was a NO-GO produced by a statistic that returned plausible output from zero information. define_froi chooses which vertices the paper's number comes from, and here it returns a contiguous, spatially plausible strip of a Glasser parcel from a localizer carrying no information, with nothing in the run log saying so. CLAUDE.md rule 5 and the project's stated signature bug class are exactly silent failure. The guard is two lines. It clears "produces a silent wrong result" if triggered, and the S2 plan's exemplar-splitting code is the realistic place a same-array copy-paste happens.

NUMPY-VERSION CONCERN IS THE WEAK PART: I tested np.argsort(np.zeros(n)) at n = 5, 10, 58, 104, 120, 1000, 10000 — identity in every case on 2.5.1. More importantly the concern is misframed: if the contrast is constant, the selection is meaningless whichever indices come back, so pinning the tie order does not make the result correct. The defect is the missing guard, not the sort kind. Do not sell this as a reproducibility bug.

SEVERITY: minor is correctly calibrated. Real, verified, silent, cheap to fix, but gated behind a caller bug and incapable of fabricating a positive. I am not raising it.
correction:
Narrowed version that should be fixed:

`define_froi` (roi_stats.py:499, operative line `keep = pv[np.argsort(sel)[::-1][:k]]`) performs no validation that the localizer contrast carries information. When `sel` is constant it silently returns the last `k` positions of `parcel_verts` as given — a contiguous, spatially plausible strip. Consequence is a wrong-region fROI and a spurious NO-GO, NOT an inflated p-value: the fROI is still test-data-independent, so it cannot manufacture selectivity.

Drop from the finding: (1) the line number 388 (it is 499); (2) "highest vertex indices" as stated — the invariant is positional (tail of parcel_verts in its given order); it only reads as highest-index because Glasser parcels are passed sorted; (3) the NumPy-version-drift argument — argsort of an all-tied array is identity at every size I tested, and a constant contrast makes the tie order irrelevant anyway. Sorting stability is not the issue; the missing guard is.

The proposed fix as written BREAKS A PASSING TEST. tests/test_roi_stats.py:407-409, `test_define_froi_caps_at_parcel_size`, deliberately calls `define_froi(np.zeros(10), np.zeros(10), parcel, top_n=100)` to exercise the top_n cap. Adding `if np.ptp(sel) == 0: raise ValueError(...)` turns that test red. Any fix must rewrite that test to use a non-degenerate contrast in the same change. All 32 tests pass today.

STRENGTHENING — same root cause, strictly more damaging, no caller bug required. `np.argsort` places NaN LAST in ascending order, so `[::-1]` places it FIRST. Any NaN in the localizer contrast makes define_froi preferentially select exactly the invalid vertices. Verified: with NaNs seeded at vertices 3, 7, 11, 50, 99 in loc_a and otherwise random normal data, define_froi(..., top_n=10) returned [2, 3, 7, 11, 33, 50, 73, 99, 108, 113] — all five NaN vertices in the top ten. `grep -n "nan\|NaN" tribe_tools/roi_stats.py` returns nothing: the module has no NaN handling anywhere. I found no confirmed NaN source in the current pipeline (TRIBE outputs are float32 from a net; glm_contrast_z already guards zero-variance to 0), so this is a latent hazard rather than an active bug — but unlike the tie case it needs no copy-paste error, and if the localizer NaNs while the test data does not, downstream numbers come back finite and honest-looking for a region chosen by invalidity.

Suggested guard covering both, placed after `sel = a[pv] - b[pv]`:
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(sel)):
        raise ValueError("localizer contrast contains non-finite values")
    if np.ptp(sel) == 0:
        raise ValueError("localizer contrast is constant - no selectivity to rank")
plus `order = np.argsort(-sel, kind="stable")` for a pinned, documented tie order, and a warning when sel[order[k-1]] == sel[order[k]] so an arbitrary cut is at least logged.
